translation_en: Qutaybah ibn Said and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Hatim (Ibn Ismail) narrated to us, from al-Muhajir ibn Mismar, from Amir ibn Sad ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: I sent my servant Nafi to Jabir ibn Samurah with a message asking him to tell me something he had heard from the Messenger of Allah. He wrote back: I heard the Messenger of Allah say on a Friday evening, the day al-Aslami was stoned: The religion will remain established until the Hour comes, or until there are twelve caliphs over you, all from Quraysh. I heard him say: A band of Muslims will conquer the White House, the house of Khosrow or the family of Khosrow. I heard him say: Before the Hour there will be liars, so beware of them. I heard him say: When Allah grants one of you good, let him begin with himself and his household. I heard him say: I will be the first to arrive at the Pool.

Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to us: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us: Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from al-Muhajir ibn Mismar, from Amir ibn Sad, who sent a message to Ibn Samurah al-Adawi asking him to tell them what he had heard from the Messenger of Allah. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say... Then he mentioned a report similar to Hatim's hadith.

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-Ala narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Ibn Umar, who said: I was present with my father when he was struck down. People praised him and said: May Allah reward you well. He said: I am both hopeful and fearful. They said: Appoint a successor. He said: Shall I bear responsibility for your affairs both alive and dead? I wish my share of it were just enough, with neither burden nor reward for me. If I appoint a successor, someone better than me appointed one before me, meaning Abu Bakr. If I leave you, someone better than me left you, the Messenger of Allah. Abdullah said: When he mentioned the Messenger of Allah, I knew that he would not appoint a successor.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Ibn Abi Umar, Muhammad ibn Rafi, and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us; their wordings are close. Ishaq and Abd said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us. The other two said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; Mamar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim informed me, from Ibn Umar, who said: I visited Hafsah, and she said: Do you know that your father is not appointing a successor? I said: He would not do that. She said: He is going to do it. I swore that I would speak to him about it, but I remained silent until morning and did not speak to him. It felt as though I were carrying a mountain on my right hand until I returned and entered upon him. He asked me about the people's condition, and I told him. Then I said: I have heard people say something, and I swore I would tell you. They claim you are not appointing a successor. If you had a camel herder or sheep herder who came to you after leaving his herd, you would think he had neglected it. Caring for the people is more serious. He agreed with what I said, lowered his head for a while, then raised it to me and said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will preserve His religion. If I do not appoint a successor, the Messenger of Allah did not appoint one; and if I do appoint one, Abu Bakr appointed one. By Allah, as soon as he mentioned the Messenger of Allah and Abu Bakr, I knew he would not consider anyone equal to the Messenger of Allah and that he would not appoint a successor.

Abd al-Malik ibn Shuaib ibn al-Layth narrated to us: My father, Shuaib ibn al-Layth, narrated to me: al-Layth ibn Sad narrated to me: Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to me, from Bakr ibn Amr, from al-Harith ibn Yazid al-Hadrami, from Ibn Hujayrah al-Akbar, from Abu Dharr, who said: I said: Messenger of Allah, will you not appoint me to a position? He struck my shoulder with his hand, then said: Abu Dharr, you are weak, and this responsibility is a trust. On the Day of Resurrection it will be disgrace and regret, except for one who takes it with its due right and fulfills the obligations it entails.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, both from al-Muqri. Zuhayr said: Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us: Said ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us, from Ubaydullah ibn Abi Jafar al-Qurashi, from Salim ibn Abi Salim al-Jayshani, from his father, from Abu Dharr, that the Messenger of Allah said: Abu Dharr, I see that you are weak, and I want for you what I want for myself. Do not take authority over even two people, and do not take charge of an orphan's property.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ibn Numayr narrated to us. They said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr (Ibn Dinar), from Amr ibn Aws, from Abdullah ibn Amr. Ibn Numayr and Abu Bakr attribute it to the Prophet; in Zuhayr's report he said that the Messenger of Allah said: Those who are just will be on pulpits of light at the right hand of the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic, and both His hands are right hands: those who act justly in their judgments, with their families, and in what they are responsible for.

Harun ibn Said al-Ayli narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Harmalah narrated to me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Shumasah, who said: I came to Aishah to ask her about something. She asked: Where are you from? I said: I am a man from Egypt. She asked: How did your leader treat you in this campaign of yours? He said: We found no fault with him. If a man's camel died, he gave him a camel; if a slave died, he gave him a slave; and if someone needed provisions, he gave him provisions. She said: What he did to my brother Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr will not prevent me from telling you what I heard the Messenger of Allah say in this house of mine: O Allah, whoever is given authority over any affair of my community and makes things difficult for them, make things difficult for him; and whoever is given authority over any affair of my community and treats them gently, treat him gently.

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from Harmalah al-Misri, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Shumasah, from Aishah, from the Prophet, with a report similar to it.

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us: Layth narrated to us. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet, who said: Each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock. The leader over the people is a shepherd and is responsible for his flock. A man is a shepherd over his household and is responsible for them. A woman is a shepherd over her husband's home and children and is responsible for them. A servant is a shepherd over his master's property and is responsible for it. So each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us. [Other chains:] Ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us; Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Khalid (Ibn al-Harith) narrated to us; Ubaydullah ibn Said narrated to us: Yahya (al-Qattan) narrated to us. All report it from Ubaydullah ibn Umar. [Another chain:] Abu al-Rabi and Abu Kamil narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us. [Another chain:] Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ismail narrated to us. All report it from Ayyub. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to me: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us: al-Dahhak (Ibn Uthman) informed us. [Another chain:] Harun ibn Said al-Ayli narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Usamah narrated to me. All report it from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, with a hadith like Layth's report from Nafi. Abu Ishaq said: al-Hasan ibn Bishr narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Ubaydullah, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, with a report like Layth's from Nafi.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah ibn Said, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us, all from Ismail ibn Jafar, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar, who said that the Messenger of Allah said... [Another chain:] Harmalah ibn Yahya informed me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn Abdullah, from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say something with the meaning of Nafi's report from Ibn Umar. Al-Zuhri's hadith adds: I think he said, 'A man is a shepherd over his father's property and is responsible for his flock.'

Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to me: My uncle Abdullah ibn Wahb informed me: A man whose name he mentioned, and Amr ibn al-Harith, informed me, from Bukayr, from Busr ibn Said, who narrated to him, from Abdullah ibn Umar, from the Prophet, with this meaning.

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us: al-Hasan narrated to us that Aidh ibn Amr, one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, entered upon Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad and said: My son, I heard the Messenger of Allah say: The worst shepherds are the harsh ones, so beware of being one of them. He said to him: Sit down. You are only the dregs of Muhammad's Companions. Aidh replied: Was there dross among them? Dross appeared after them, among others.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ismail ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan, from Abu Zurah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: One day the Messenger of Allah stood among us, mentioned misappropriation from the spoils, and spoke gravely about it and its seriousness. Then he said: Let me not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel on his neck, groaning, and saying: Messenger of Allah, help me! I will have no power to do anything for you; I already conveyed the message to you. Let me not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a horse on his neck, neighing, and saying: Messenger of Allah, help me! I will have no power to do anything for you; I already conveyed the message to you. Let me not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a sheep on his neck, bleating, and saying: Messenger of Allah, help me! I will have no power to do anything for you; I already conveyed the message to you. Let me not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a person on his neck, crying out, and saying: Messenger of Allah, help me! I will have no power to do anything for you; I already conveyed the message to you. Let me not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with fluttering pieces of cloth on his neck, and saying: Messenger of Allah, help me! I will have no power to do anything for you; I already conveyed the message to you. Let me not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with something silent on his neck, and saying: Messenger of Allah, help me! I will say: I have no power to do anything for you; I already conveyed the message to you.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan. [Another chain:] Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan and Umarah ibn al-Qaqa, both from Abu Zurah, from Abu Hurayrah, with a report like Ismail's narration from Abu Hayyan.

Ahmad ibn Said ibn Sakhr al-Darimi narrated to me: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us: Hammad (Ibn Zayd) narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Yahya ibn Said, from Abu Zurah ibn Amr ibn Jarir, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah mentioned misappropriation from the spoils and spoke gravely of it. He related the hadith. Hammad said: Then I later heard Yahya narrate it, and he narrated to us something like what Ayyub had narrated to us from him.

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Khirash narrated to me: Abu Mamar narrated to us: Abd al-Warith narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Said ibn Hayyan, from Abu Zurah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, with a report similar to theirs.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Amr al-Naqid, and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us; the wording is Abu Bakr's. They said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Abu Humayd al-Saidi, who said: The Messenger of Allah appointed a man from the Azd, called Ibn al-Lutbiyyah, to collect charity. Amr and Ibn Abi Umar said: to collect charity. When he returned, he said: This is for you, and this was given to me as a gift. The Messenger of Allah stood on the pulpit, praised Allah, and said: What is the matter with an official whom I send out, who then says, 'This is for you, and this was given to me as a gift'? Why did he not sit in his father's or mother's house and see whether he would be given a gift or not? By the One in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, none of you takes anything from it except that he will bring it on the Day of Resurrection carried on his neck: a camel groaning, a cow mooing, or a sheep bleating. Then he raised his hands until we saw the whiteness of his armpits and said twice: O Allah, have I conveyed the message?

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Abd ibn Humayd said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Mamar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Abu Humayd al-Saidi, who said: The Prophet appointed Ibn al-Lutbiyyah, a man from the Azd, to collect charity. He brought the property and handed it to the Prophet, saying: This is your property, and this is a gift given to me. The Prophet said to him: Why did you not sit in your father's and mother's house and see whether you would be given a gift or not? Then the Prophet stood to deliver a sermon and mentioned a report like Sufyan's hadith.

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-Ala narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Humayd al-Saidi, who said: The Messenger of Allah appointed a man from the Azd, called Ibn al-Utbiyyah, to collect the charity of Banu Sulaym. When he came back, he audited him. The man said: This is your property, and this was given to me as a gift. The Messenger of Allah said: Why did you not stay in your father's and mother's house until your gift came to you, if you are telling the truth? Then he addressed us, praised Allah, and said: To proceed: I appoint one of you to a task Allah has entrusted to me, and he comes back saying, 'This is your property, and this was given to me as a gift.' Why did he not stay in his father's and mother's house until his gift came to him, if he is telling the truth? By Allah, none of you takes anything from it without right except that he will meet Allah Most High carrying it on the Day of Resurrection. I will surely recognize one of you meeting Allah carrying a camel that groans, a cow that moos, or a sheep that bleats. Then he raised his hands until the whiteness of his armpits was visible and said: O Allah, have I conveyed the message? My eyes saw it and my ears heard it.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abdah, Ibn Numayr, and Abu Muawiyah narrated to us. [Another chain:] Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us. [Another chain:] Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us. All report it from Hisham with this chain. In Abdah's and Ibn Numayr's narration, it says: When he returned, he audited him, as Abu Usamah said. Ibn Numayr's version says: By Allah, you will surely know that none of you takes anything from it. Sufyan's narration adds: My eyes saw it and my ears heard it. And ask Zayd ibn Thabit, for he was present with me.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Jarir informed us, from al-Shaybani, from Abdullah ibn Dhakwan (Abu al-Zinad), from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, that the Messenger of Allah appointed a man to collect charity. He returned with a large amount and kept saying: This is for you, and this was given to me as a gift. He mentioned a report similar to it. Urwah said: I asked Abu Humayd al-Saidi: Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah? He said: From his mouth to my ear.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us: Ismail ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Adi ibn Amirah al-Kindi, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: If we appoint one of you to a task and he conceals from us even a needle, or anything above it, that is misappropriation which he will bring on the Day of Resurrection. A dark-skinned man from the Ansar stood up—I can almost see him—and said: Messenger of Allah, relieve me of your appointment. He asked: What is the matter with you? The man said: I heard you say such-and-such. He said: I say it now too: Whoever among you is appointed by us to a task must bring back everything, little or much. Whatever he is given, he may take; whatever he is forbidden, he must refrain from.

Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated this to us: My father and Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to me: Abu Usamah narrated to us. They said: Ismail narrated to us with this chain and a report like it.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated this to us: al-Fadl ibn Musa informed us: Ismail ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us: Qays ibn Abi Hazim informed us, who said: I heard Adi ibn Amirah al-Kindi say: I heard the Messenger of Allah say something like their hadith.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Harun ibn Abdullah narrated to me: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: The verse 'O you who believe, obey Allah, obey the Messenger, and those in authority among you' (Quran 4:59) was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Hudhafah ibn Qays ibn Adi al-Sahmi, whom the Prophet sent with a detachment. Yala ibn Muslim informed me of this, from Said ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas.

Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: al-Mughirah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hizami informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah. Whoever obeys the commander has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys the commander has disobeyed me. Zuhayr ibn Harb also narrated this to me: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad with this chain, but did not mention: 'Whoever disobeys the commander has disobeyed me.'

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah. Whoever obeys my commander has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys my commander has disobeyed me.

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from Ziyad, from Ibn Shihab, that Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman informed him that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah said the same.
